_comment: Machine-readable half of the fork merge inventory. Paths, verdicts, tripwires
and convergence rules live HERE and nowhere else; upstream-merge-inventory.md
carries the narrative that cannot be checked (the re-application Deltas, the
Every path in this file is checked against upstream/main and HEAD by
catches an entry going stale: an `ours` path upstream has started shipping, or
a `decide`/`converged` path upstream renamed out from under a fork delta.
Run it before every merge; it is step 0 of the skill.

verdicts.ours: Take the fork side wholesale. Legitimate ONLY when the path does not exist in upstream/main.
verdicts.theirs-verbatim: Take upstream exactly, and investigate why a fork delta reappeared.
verdicts.converged: Take upstream wholesale, then re-apply only the listed fork delta.
verdicts.decide: No cached verdict. Read upstream's side every merge and decide it there.

concerns.name: Authentication and session
concerns.forkPosition: Moatless cookie session and /login; no T3 backend session.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Do not adopt upstream auth work.

concerns.name: Client / device identity
concerns.upstreamAddition: Do not adopt; check deleted surfaces.

concerns.name: Dev-server origin and proxy
concerns.forkPosition: Upstream single-origin dev plus fork proxy-target override.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Adopt upstream, then re-apply the fork delta.

concerns.name: Backend contract
concerns.forkPosition: The client may assume only what Moatless implements; see docs/internals/client-server-contract.md.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Adopt only if Moatless implements it.

concerns.name: Electron / desktop
concerns.forkPosition: Kept in tree; not a compliance target.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Take upstream; do not spend merge effort making desktop work.

sweep.note: Widen the pattern when a concern grows vocabulary it does not cover. Keyword hits are a starting list, not a verdict — most are false positives and are recorded as such in the tracker.

offRepo.note: Every other workflow inherited from upstream is disabled in GitHub, not in the tree. A workflow upstream adds later arrives active, so this check fails AFTER a merge rather than before one. Disable a new one with: gh workflow disable <name> --repo soaplabs/t3code

deletedUpstreamPaths.note: Upstream owns these and the fork's side is deletion. An upstream edit raises a delete/modify conflict, and taking upstream silently restores the file. The tripwire script asserts this list is exactly what `git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only upstream/main HEAD` reports.

pathPolicy.note: Keep the Moatless cookie session. Upstream owns this file and changes the environment layer around it; take those changes and re-state the fork's session behavior on top.
Keep cookie session behavior and the absent same-origin gate. Take upstream's transport changes.
Fork-only /login.
Keep fork auth coverage. Upstream owns this file; take its harness and assertion changes and keep the fork's cases beside them.
Take upstream, then apply Web Vite Delta.

CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it. Keep the fork's slimmed shape and its This fork section. Upstream owns and edits this file: read its version for new facts — surfaces, commands, paths, sharp edges — and re-state those in the fork's voice rather than taking upstream's prose.
Fork docs, this inventory, the tracker and the gaps register.
The fork's two skills: merging upstream, and testing the web client against a Moatless backend. Upstream owns the other skills in .agents/skills/ and adds more.

Take theirs, then re-apply the scope note at the top of each. Both describe the bundled T3 server, which the fork's web client does not use; the note is a few lines routing readers to test-moatless-web and is deliberately the whole delta, so upstream's edits to these docs land unopposed.
Fork-authored user and internals docs.
The four fork-authored plans. The first three verified 2026-08-03, the fourth written in this fork on 2026-08-05.

Everything under .plans/ except the four fork-authored plans above. Upstream owns most files here and adds more. This entry was `ours` until 2026-08-03, which would have discarded every upstream plan edit.
Take upstream exactly; investigate any re-grown fork delta.

Thread-server and sandbox lifecycle surfaces. None of these exist upstream. The thread-server UI components listed here until 2026-08-08 (apps/web/src/components/servers/**, added in #13) are gone; what renders a ThreadServer now lives under components/preview/ and is covered by fork-preview-files.
The last two are the host half of the preview annotation protocol for a framed page — upstream annotates over ipcRenderer into a <webview> preload and has no postMessage equivalent to converge on.
Everything under browser/ except the fork-only files above. Take upstream and re-state the hosted-preview behavior from the Hosted web preview inventory entry on top.

Each renders or reasons about ThreadServer, a Moatless concept upstream does not have. PreviewFrameMoreMenu.tsx is a deliberate sibling of upstream's PreviewMoreMenu.tsx, not a fork of it — keep upstream's file at zero delta.

Everything under components/preview/ except the fork-only files above. Take upstream and re-state the hosted-preview behavior on top. PreviewEmptyState.tsx, PreviewView.tsx and PreviewChromeRow.test.tsx are upstream's files carrying fork deltas.
Take upstream, then re-apply UnsupportedMethodError, its unsupported-method error unions, and servers.* wiring. Recompute the unions — never hand-edit.
Take upstream, then re-add the hosted-environment method entries: servers.*, sandbox.status, sandbox.start, and sandbox.stop.
The surface-gating registry and the mobile touch modules.
Fork-only mapping from a message origin to its chip. Written for a concept upstream does not have.
Take upstream, then apply Message Origin Delta. MessagesTimeline.tsx is a file upstream works in steadily; the delta is additive and must not re-indent upstream blocks.

Take upstream, then apply Mobile Touch Delta. Sidebar.tsx (upstream's default sidebar since 2026-08-08, formerly SidebarV2.tsx) also carries the Navigation gates and PR-driven settling deltas; all must survive.
Fork-only workflows.
The one exception to the entry below. Take upstream, then re-apply the single `Check the Moatless API description is current` step in the check job. Nothing else in this file is fork-owned.

Everything else under .github/workflows/. Upstream's files byte for byte, including workflows upstream adds later. They are switched off in GitHub, not in the tree, so there is no delta to preserve. Any fork delta here means someone edited a workflow — investigate before taking it.

inventory.name: Moatless cookie session
inventory.mustSurvive: The browser authenticates by Moatless cookie session, there is no T3 backend session exchange, and /login is the entry point. Only login.tsx is fork-only; the other three are decide — upstream owns them and keeps changing the environment layer they sit in.

inventory.name: Proxy target, allowed hosts, dev pins
inventory.mustSurvive: Converged; apply only Web Vite Delta.

inventory.name: Upstream workflows switched off
inventory.mustSurvive: No workflow inherited from upstream runs in this fork. Enforced in GitHub as state: disabled_manually, not in the tree — see offRepo.

inventory.name: Agent instructions
inventory.mustSurvive: The file says this is a fork of pingdotgg/t3code, what the fork changes, and that fork-upstream-merge governs ownership questions; and it stays short enough to be read in full. It also carries the fork's surgical-change rules: fork code says so in a comment, and reaches upstream files through an additive hook. Resolve conflicts by fact, not by hunk.

inventory.name: Fork documentation and plans
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep ours. Only those four plans are ours; upstream owns the rest of .plans/**, and only fork-upstream-merge and test-moatless-web are ours under .agents/skills/.

inventory.name: Hosted-environment contract group
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep fork methods: server list, server status subscription, server log subscription, sandbox status, sandbox status subscription, sandbox start, and sandbox stop. Keep sandbox lifecycle schemas separate from server list schemas. sandbox.subscribeStatus is gated on the sandboxStatusPush capability: absent, the client polls sandbox.status instead, so both paths have to keep working.

inventory.name: Server state in client runtime
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep fork server and sandbox lifecycle state surfaces separate. sandbox exposes both status (polled query, the fallback) and statusStream (the pushed subscription); dropping either leaves one class of server without a live indicator. The subscription tag is also listed in EnvironmentSubscriptionRpcTag in rpc/client.ts, an upstream file.

inventory.name: Servers view in right panel
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep fork UI unless upstream ships an equivalent. The dedicated components/servers/ directory is gone — server rendering folded into components/preview/.

inventory.name: Hosted web preview
inventory.mustSurvive: Preview renders in a hosted iframe rather than a native browser surface, and a frame that loaded before its server was serving is replaced when the server reaches started (useFramedServerReload in PreviewView.tsx — a webview reloads itself, a frame does not). Upstream owns most files and works in them; take upstream and re-state the iframe behavior on top. Also surviving (2026-08-07): a framed page can be annotated — four gates on the existing framed flag in PreviewView.tsx, each // Fork: marked and additive. Drop the whole delta once upstream ships a web preview.

inventory.name: Upstream-server hosted-env stubs
inventory.mustSurvive: Converged; re-add servers.*, sandbox.status, sandbox.start, and sandbox.stop entries. Drop these first if upstream ships server-shaped support.

inventory.name: Sandbox lifecycle controls
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep the start/status control and right-panel disabling until upstream has an environment lifecycle capability the web client can use. The control renders inside the panel body — under the launcher's surface cards, and under the disabled state's reason where it is the only way back up — not in the tab bar, whose right end belongs to upstream's layout toggles. useSandboxAvailability picks the pushed subscription over the polled read on the sandboxStatusPush capability; without one of the two the indicator goes stale the moment a sandbox moves while the panel is open.

inventory.name: UnsupportedMethodError
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep error class until upstream has optional/unsupported method semantics.

inventory.name: Unsupported-method error unions
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep one entry per Moatless-unserved method. Recompute with scripts/unsupported-methods.mjs; never hand-edit.

inventory.name: Surface-gating registry
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep as the only source of fork surface flags. Unknown route/action keys default enabled; tests must read upstream keys rather than restating them.

inventory.name: Chat surface gates
inventory.mustSurvive: Re-apply additive gates only. PanelLayoutControls.tsx left this entry when the fork took the terminal-drawer button back: the file is upstream's byte for byte again, so a merge has nothing to re-apply there.

inventory.name: Persisted panel gating
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep migrate disposal for hidden/unknown surfaces. The fork's generic unknown-kind drop subsumes upstream's per-kind removals.

inventory.name: Mobile touch affordances
inventory.mustSurvive: The left sidebar is a drawer the finger drags in from the screen edge, and a long press on a thread row reaches Settle, Snooze, rename and archive. The three fork/ modules are ours; the four upstream files are converged — see Mobile Touch Delta. The drawer must not become a modal <dialog>: that makes document.body inert, and the menus it exists to open portal there.

inventory.name: Message origin
inventory.mustSurvive: A message that reached the thread through an adapter or from another Task says so, and a message typed into the composer renders exactly as upstream renders it. The contract field is optional rather than nullable so the absent case stays byte-identical to upstream's payload.

inventory.name: Host-run project scripts
inventory.mustSurvive: scripts.run asks the environment to run a project's script in its own sandbox, hosted in a named terminal, returning that terminal and the URL of any port it publishes. Gated on the workspaceScripts capability: absent, runProjectScript keeps upstream's client-driven terminal.open + terminal.write path byte-for-byte, so a T3 server behaves exactly as upstream. The rpc.ts union entry is the one documented exception to unsupported-methods.mjs's DROP advice — it is upstream's OWN server that refuses this method, not Moatless, so the derivation reports it backwards once the backend half publishes. Keep it while apps/server answers with UnsupportedMethodError; see 'A script runs on the backend' in gaps.md. A SandboxNotRunningError from scripts.run is answered rather than reported: startSandboxForScript starts the thread's sandbox, polls sandbox.status until ready, and re-runs once. Upstream has nothing to start, so a merge that loses this turns an idle-reaped sandbox back into a dead end.

inventory.name: Project-script editing capability
inventory.mustSurvive: A project's scripts can be edited only when the backend says so per workspace: a git-synced workspace owns its scripts in .moatless/workspaces.json and is projected read-only, a manual one is writable. That answer rides the wire as scriptsEditable on OrchestrationProject / OrchestrationProjectShell, threaded to ProjectScriptsControl and ProjectSettingsPanel as an `editable` prop that gates the per-script Edit button, the t3.json import items and the Add action. It is NOT a FEATURES flag — projectScriptEditing was deleted when the capability arrived, because the answer varies per deployment and per workspace. Running a script stays ungated: a read-only workspace still runs what it declares, and ProjectScriptsControl's no-primary-script branch returns null only when editing is also off. A merge that reintroduces FEATURES.projectScriptEditing or an always-on Add action has taken upstream's side back.

inventory.name: Project-script port field
inventory.mustSurvive: The script editor sets a numeric Port, not upstream's free-text Preview URL: a script in a remote sandbox has no localhost to point at, so the host publishes the port and returns the real external URL when the script runs (scripts.run). ProjectScript carries port (1..65535); the editor's Port input replaces the Preview URL input and auto-open toggle, and buildProjectScript derives autoOpenPreview from the port's presence. previewUrl / autoOpenPreview stay on the contract for wire-compatibility but the fork's UI never writes a URL. A merge that restores the Preview URL input has dropped the port.

inventory.name: Moatless branding
inventory.mustSurvive: The client names itself Moatless, not T3 Code. APP_BASE_NAME falls back to "Moatless" where upstream falls back to "T3 Code", index.html carries the Moatless title and splash labels, and SidebarBrand renders APP_BASE_NAME in place of upstream's T3Wordmark SVG plus its "Code" span — the T3Wordmark function is deleted with it. Everything downstream of APP_BASE_NAME (window title, version-skew copy, auth shells) follows from the one constant, so only these four files carry the delta. Upstream restyles the brand row regularly: take upstream's markup and keep the one APP_BASE_NAME span.

inventory.name: Server-update banner gate
inventory.mustSurvive: The composer never offers to run T3's self-update: the Moatless server does not implement server.updateServer, so the offer and its npx t3 command would point at a command that cannot run. One additive FEATURES.serverUpdateBanner gate on upstream's composer-banner line. Holds open the Desktop and host lifecycle gap. Drop the flag and gate once the backend serves server.updateServer.

inventory.name: PR-driven settling gate
inventory.mustSurvive: A pull request never decides whether a thread is settled — neither merged/closed settling one nor open holding one out of the shelf. Two additive FEATURES.prThreadSettling gates feed effectiveSettled a null changeRequestState; effectiveSettled itself is upstream's and unmodified. A merge that finds a thread settling on a merged PR has taken upstream's side back.

inventory.name: Navigation gates
inventory.mustSurvive: Re-apply list filtering gates.

inventory.name: Thread deletion gate in the row menu
inventory.mustSurvive: The row menu never offers Delete: orchestration.dispatchCommand is dispatched as one method, so a thread.delete Moatless does not implement fails generically after the user has already asked for it. One additive FEATURES.threadDeletion spread around upstream's delete item in buildThreadActionMenuItems, which makes archive the tail of the menu — upstream's tests assume delete is. Archive itself is upstream's since 2026-08-16 and is no longer a fork delta.

inventory.name: Settings gates
inventory.mustSurvive: Re-apply route guard and nav/search filtering. General, Appearance, and Providers stay visible except the server-backed add-provider-instance affordance, which lives in ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx since upstream extracted it on 2026-08-08.

inventory.name: Moatless REST client
inventory.mustSurvive: Fork-only. The generated client for the Moatless REST API, plus the checked-in OpenAPI description it is generated from and the CI check that the two have not drifted. Regenerate with `vp run --filter @t3tools/moatless-api generate`; do not hand-edit src/generated/**. customInstance.ts carries an @effect-diagnostics-next-line globalFetch:off — the package is deliberately outside Effect.

inventory.name: Moatless administration reads
inventory.mustSurvive: Fork-only. Caching and dirty-form helpers for the administration pages. Deliberately not createEnvironmentQueryAtomFamily: that helper waits on the environment socket, and administration data is plain HTTP that has no reason to blank on a reconnect. If upstream ships a socket-independent query helper, prefer it and delete query.ts.

inventory.name: Moatless administration pages
inventory.mustSurvive: An administrator reaches every Moatless administration surface from T3 settings — Workspaces, Loops, Integrations, Skills, Secrets and Users, each with its detail route. Built out of upstream's own settings primitives (SettingsSection, SettingsRow, itemRows), so upstream restyling reaches them for free — keep it that way. See the inventory markdown for the markup conventions.

inventory.name: Moatless administration nav and guard
inventory.mustSurvive: Converged with Settings gates; the same files carry both deltas and both must survive. Additive: the Administration nav group, the MOATLESS_ADMIN_PATHS entries, the beforeLoad redirect for a non-administrator, and an export on normalizeSearchText. The guard matches detail routes by path prefix — a new administration route with children must be added to MOATLESS_ADMIN_PATHS or it is reachable without an admin check.

convergence.name: Auth
convergence.watchFor: No convergence expected; auth is fork-owned.

convergence.name: Dev proxy / single-origin
convergence.watchFor: Work on DEV_PROXIED_PATH_PREFIXES, T3CODE_SINGLE_ORIGIN_DEV, or resolveDevProxyTarget.
convergence.action: Take upstream and re-apply only Web Vite Delta.

convergence.name: Allowed hosts
convergence.action: Drop the T3CODE_ALLOWED_HOSTS alias once deployments inject upstream's name.

convergence.name: Thread servers
convergence.watchFor: Any upstream concept of a server owned by a thread, especially in WS_METHODS.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream; remove fork group, stubs first.

convergence.name: Unsupported methods
convergence.watchFor: An optional-method marker, handshake metadata, ServerConfig, or an HTTP metadata endpoint — a general way for a server to say it does not serve a method.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream semantics and collapse the error-union entries into it.

convergence.name: Surface gating
convergence.watchFor: New booleans on ExecutionEnvironmentCapabilities. Upstream adds one per thread-lifecycle surface — threadSettlement, threadSnooze, threadPinning and threadPinReorder as of 2026-08-08.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream's capability where one exists and delete the matching FEATURES flag. The server decides, so the surface then follows the backend without a fork edit.

convergence.name: Web on a phone
convergence.watchFor: A swipeable mobile sidebar, a touch affordance for thread-row actions, or a contextMenuFallback rewritten on a popup primitive.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream and drop the matching part of Mobile Touch Delta.

convergence.name: Send while a turn is running
convergence.watchFor: Upstream widening showSendWhileRunning past isMobileViewport in ChatComposer.tsx, or dropping the prop and always rendering send beside stop.
convergence.action: Take upstream. The fork's own rule was dropped on 2026-08-16 when upstream shipped the prop; a phone browser is a mobile viewport, so the fork's case is served.

convergence.name: PR-driven settling
convergence.watchFor: Moatless reporting the change request for the checkout's own ref (matching headRef to refName), or upstream keying resolveThreadPr on something stronger than a branch name.
convergence.action: Delete the prThreadSettling flag and both gates; upstream's rule is correct once the PR is the thread's own.

convergence.name: Message provenance
convergence.watchFor: Any upstream field on OrchestrationMessage saying a message did not come from the composer — an origin, author, or source.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream's shape, re-point the chip at it, and drop the fork field.

convergence.name: Searchable settings list
convergence.watchFor: Upstream lifting the expandable header search out of KeybindingsSettings.tsx into a shared settings component, or giving SettingsSection a search affordance of its own.
